answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked bond: every agent must stake capital in a shared vault before it can transact, and rewards rise sublinearly with stake. An attacker who clones identities must pour funds through a narrow inlet, so splitting a budget across a thousand keys earns less than one honest large bond while locking the same money. Any identity caught faking work is slashed, and the forfeited stake flows to the peers watching from the terrace who attested it, turning each fake account into a paid liability rather than a cheap multiplier.
